properties.areaDesc: Kent; Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 4:02AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...From 8 AM this morning to 2 PM EDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.areaDesc: Kaibab Plateau; Marble and Glen Canyons; Grand Canyon Country; Coconino Plateau; Yavapai County Mountains; Western Mogollon Rim; Eastern Mogollon Rim; Northern Gila County; Yavapai County Valleys and Basins; Oak Creek and Sycamore Canyons
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 12 at 12:31AM MST until October 12 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...western Coconino, northern Gila, far southern Navajo, and
Yavapai counties.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms are expected to
continue across the are through tonight. With tropical moisture
in place from the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel and already
saturated grounds, periods of embedded heavy rainfall will be
possible which could lead to flash flooding. Additionally, the
extended period of rain could lead to elevated flow in creeks,
normally dry washes, and rivers.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Tutuila and Aunuu; Manua; Swains Island; Rose Atoll
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 11 at 7:58PM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by midweek. This trough should remain
strong and active while over the territory, and may even intensify
with embedded low pressure centers. Widespread showers may be
heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of
thunderstorms. Widespread flash flooding may occur from this
rainfall, and landslides will be possible along steep mountainous
terrain. Impacts could begin as early as Wednesday and are
expected to persist through the weekend. While there is still
uncertainty in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan
now for wet conditions that could start as early as Wednesday and
persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Wednesday through Sunday
